note: Document- and lineage-level identity for the LHC black-hole safety corpus. This case is a near-settled question, so the interesting structure is dependency depth rather than disagreement: how much of the public reassurance traces back to one institutional assessment.

cern-lsag-safety-assessment-2008.label: CERN LHC Safety Assessment Group report (2008)
cern-lsag-safety-assessment-2008.description: The institutional safety assessment. CERN's public-facing FAQ and most downstream reassurance are restatements of this one document, not independent confirmations of it.

plaga-critique-2008.label: Plaga residual-risk critique (2008)
plaga-critique-2008.description: Independent critique of the LSAG position. Responds to LSAG, so it is not independent of it as an input, but it is an independent analytical voice.

doctrine-labs-inference.label: Doctrine Labs agent inference
doctrine-labs-inference.description: Hypotheses generated by this tool. Never evidence.

https://arxiv.org/abs/0806.3414.author: LHC Safety Assessment Group, CERN
https://arxiv.org/abs/0806.3414.independence_note: The load-bearing document for the entire safety case. Three excerpts here (cosmic-ray argument, conclusion, micro-black-hole treatment) are one source making one argument, not three converging lines.

https://home.cern/science/accelerators/l.title: The safety of the LHC
https://home.cern/science/accelerators/l.author: CERN

https://home.cern/science/accelerators/l.independence_note: Same institution, same underlying assessment. Citing both CERN's page and the LSAG report is citing one source twice.

https://arxiv.org/abs/0808.1415.title: On the potential catastrophic risk from metastable quantum-black holes produced at particle colliders
https://arxiv.org/abs/0808.1415.author: Rainer Plaga
https://arxiv.org/abs/0808.1415.derivation_basis: Written as a critique of the LSAG safety argument.
https://arxiv.org/abs/0808.1415.independence_note: Giddings & Mangano published a rebuttal; LSAG cites the dispute. This corpus navigates the disagreement rather than adjudicating the physics.
